subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw solve direct `read`-tool binary-document token waste now with a safe unsupported-document fallback, or defer to broader document extraction/provider-native file handling?
rationale: Source inspection proves the direct fallback is still missing, but the issue proposes multiple product directions and has an open conflicting candidate PR, so automation should not choose the permanent user-visible behavior alone.

options.title: Port Safe Fallback
options.body: Add a small guard for known binary document formats in the shared `read` path and return a compact actionable unsupported-document message.

options.title: Defer To Document Work
options.body: Keep this tied to broader extraction or provider-native file handling and accept that direct `read` can still waste tokens until that work lands.

options.title: Guidance Only
options.body: Update tool description or prompting to discourage binary document reads without changing runtime behavior.

recommendation.title: Port Safe Fallback
recommendation.body: Add a small guard for known binary document formats in the shared `read` path and return a compact actionable unsupported-document message.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame ties the present read-tool files and wrapper to this area, making this the best available routing candidate from current-main history.
